summary.text: Gneiss is a common, widespread metamorphic rock made when igneous or sedimentary rock is changed by high temperature and high pressure.
It is coarse-grained and nearly always banded in alternating darker and lighter layers, yet it has only a weak tendency to split along them.
The bands form when hot rock is squeezed harder in one direction, so platy minerals line up in parallel layers at right angles to the strongest squeeze.

facts.label: Ancient example
facts.value: Acasta Gneiss, among Earth's oldest rocks

facts.label: Dark bands
facts.value: Richer in magnesium- and iron-bearing minerals

facts.label: Names by origin
facts.value: Orthogneiss from igneous rock, paragneiss from sedimentary

items.prompt: On a hike you find a rock with clear stripes of dark and light minerals, each grain big enough to see without a lens. Which rock is it most likely?
items.explain: Gneiss is a coarse-grained metamorphic rock that nearly always shows alternating darker and lighter bands.

items.prompt: What makes the darker stripes in gneiss darker than the lighter ones?
items.explain: Dark bands hold relatively more mafic minerals, rich in magnesium and iron; light bands hold more felsic minerals such as feldspar and quartz.

items.prompt: Push the top of a deck of cards one way and the bottom the other. When a similar force acts on hot rock deep underground, what does it do?

options.label: Lifts it straight to the surface

items.explain: This shearing force stretches the rock like a plastic and spreads the original material out into sheets.

items.prompt: Hot rock is squeezed hardest from above and below, and less from the sides. How will its gneiss bands lie?
items.explain: Bands develop perpendicular to the direction of greatest compression, as platy minerals rotate or recrystallize into parallel layers.

items.prompt: Augen gneiss contains oval feldspar grains, each wrapped in finer material. Its name comes from a German word. What does that word mean?
items.explain: Augen means eyes in German, after the elliptic or lens-shaped feldspar grains surrounded by finer material.

items.prompt: A banded metamorphic rock splits easily into thin flakes along its layers. Why would a geologist hesitate to call it gneiss?

options.label: Gneiss never has any visible layers
Gneiss forms only from sedimentary rock
Gneiss splits only weakly along its layers
Gneiss grains are too small to see

items.explain: Gneiss has only a weak tendency to fracture along its layers; metamorphic rock with stronger schistosity is classed as schist.
